body:
Crypto markets took another leg down today with total market cap sliding 2.78% to $2.48 trillion as risk-off sentiment dominated trading floors. The selloff accelerated into the close with $800 million in leveraged positions getting liquidated across exchanges, while Fear & Greed index dropped to 23 marking extreme fear territory. Bitcoin ETFs saw their largest outflow on record at $3.4 billion as institutional money rotated back into AI stocks that continue their relentless march higher. Volume stayed elevated at $120 billion but most of it was selling pressure as buyers stepped aside.

Bitcoin cracked below the critical $70,000 level and closed at $69,437, down 4.36% on the day and now sitting at 2-month lows. The breakdown came after Michael Saylor sale rumors spooked the market, though the bigger catalyst was Mt. Gox moving another 10,422 bitcoin worth $739 million to new wallets as the July deadline approaches. BTC dominance actually ticked up to 56.2% as altcoins got hit even harder, but this feels more like a flight to relative safety than genuine strength. Key support now sits at $68,500 with the 200-day moving average around $67,800 looming as the next major test if sellers keep pressing.

Ethereum showed surprising resilience, down just 0.19% to $1,977.68 while most majors took bigger hits. This divergence is notable given ETH typically amplifies Bitcoin moves on the downside, suggesting some underlying strength or different positioning dynamics. Solana dropped 2.41% to $79.06 while BNB fell 3.90% to $677.49, both underperforming the broader market. Cardano and XRP both shed over 3% with ADA touching $0.22 and XRP slipping below $1.30. The fact that even defensive plays like Chainlink couldn't hold green speaks to the breadth of today's weakness across the ecosystem.

The macro backdrop continues deteriorating for risk assets as the equity-crypto correlation that worked so well during the AI rally is now working in reverse. Traditional markets are showing rotation fatigue while crypto lacks its own fundamental catalysts to drive independent strength. Regulatory overhang persists with no clear timeline on major policy shifts, and the Mt. Gox distribution timeline is creating a persistent selling pressure narrative. Rate expectations remain stable but the risk-off mood in broader markets is bleeding into crypto as institutional flows turn negative.

All eyes now turn to Friday's jobs data which could shift Fed expectations and broader market sentiment. The $68,500 level on Bitcoin represents do-or-die support with a break targeting the mid-$60,000s where real accumulation typically emerges. Any positive developments around the Grayscale HYPE ETF approval could provide a counter-narrative, but for now the path of least resistance remains lower until either oversold conditions trigger a bounce or fresh institutional buying emerges. Watch for any clarity on the Mt. Gox timeline as that remains the biggest near-term overhang on market psychology.
